title.value: Diagnosing as autistic people increasingly distant from prototypes lead neither to clinical benefit nor to the advancement of knowledge
title.justification: The title directly reflects the paper's focus on the issues with broadening autism diagnoses beyond traditional prototypes, as discussed extensively throughout the paper.
title.quote: "Diagnosing as autistic people increasingly distant from prototypes lead neither to clinical benefit nor to the advancement of knowledge"

analysis.description: The paper discusses the challenges and implications of broadening the autism spectrum to include diverse phenotypes that deviate from traditional prototypes. It critiques the potential scientific and clinical downsides of increasing heterogeneity in autism diagnoses and suggests a more focused approach in research to better understand distinct subgroups within the autism spectrum.

type.justification: The paper primarily deals with theoretical perspectives on the classification and diagnosis of autism and its implications for research and clinical practice.
type.quote: "The position of Hobson and Petty [7] dominates the scientific community. It is based on the optimistic belief that science progresses in a linear fashion, whereas it actually progresses by leaps and bounds."

name.justification: The paper revolves around the psychiatric classification and understanding of autism spectrum disorders, fitting primarily into the field of Psychiatry and Autism Research.
name.quote: "We suggest first separately studying at least three groups of individuals currently lumped together within the autism spectrum..."

name.justification: The paper discusses clinical implications and critiques of current diagnostic practices in autism spectrum disorders, aligning it with Clinical Psychiatry.
name.quote: "The benefit of a diagnosis lies in the established, agreed-upon knowledge of a clinical group that can be applied to the individual..."

name.justification: The paper touches upon neurodevelopmental aspects and genetic predispositions related to autism, making it relevant to Neurodevelopmental Disorders research.
name.quote: "Another example of the deleterious effects of a historical trend toward overinclusive diagnoses is the careless assimilation into autism of autistic-like clinical presentations associated with identified genetic mutations or neurodevelopmental syndromes..."
